# PHOENIX security patch

This is a local patch of upstream `picomatch` 4.0.7 for GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf / CVE-2026-112366. It is based on the parser and regression-test changes proposed in upstream PR [micromatch/picomatch#259](https://github.com/micromatch/picomatch/pull/259), commit `3ff1db1827881700ab90efd8b5b5915d9b3dc096`. The upstream PR was closed without merging and has not been released as an npm version (the public registry still reports `4.0.7` as latest), so this PHOENIX-only fork is locally versioned `4.0.8`. This is not an upstream release; the local version is above the advisory's vulnerable range (`<=4.0.7`) so npm audit can distinguish the patched fork from the vulnerable upstream tarball.

The patch mitigates the reported repeated-extglob catastrophic-backtracking cases and adds conservative handling for nested/ambiguous repeated patterns. It does not assert that arbitrary user-controlled glob patterns are universally ReDoS-proof. The existing explicit `maxExtglobRecursion: false` opt-out disables the upstream safeguards and must not be used for attacker-controlled patterns.

The consuming app has a separate subprocess-timeout regression test at `src/test/picomatch-security.test.ts`. Reassess and replace this fork with an official upstream release once one containing a reviewed fix is published.

This update includes later changes from the proposed PR after the original local patch; that earlier patch still timed out on hostile patterns such as `+({a,a})`, `+(a|[[:alpha:]])` and `@(a|a)+`. The local version number makes the npm advisory check pass but does not independently attest to security. This unmerged patch intentionally literalizes some ambiguous patterns and may change matching semantics. Avoid untrusted glob patterns; plain regular expression groups, explicit unsafe options, and other constructs are not guaranteed safe.
